panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Axial MRI panel showing left frontal sinus lesion with wall erosion and anterior cranial fossa extension, consistent with Pott puffy tumor in an adult case series. B: Post-contrast MRI panel showing a ring-enhancing abscess-like collection with dural enhancement, a recognized intracranial complication of Pott puffy tumor. C: DWI MRI panel demonstrating restricted diffusion in the frontal collection, supporting an abscess complicating Pott puffy tumor. D: ADC map panel corresponding to the diffusion-restricted frontal abscess in Pott puffy tumor.
panels.attribution_text: Sideris et al. Pott Puffy Tumor in Adults: The Τiming of Surgical Ιntervention.. Cureus 2020. doi:10.7759/cureus.11781. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: MRI scan (Case 1) Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed enhancing lesion filling the left frontal sinus and erosion of the internal wall of the frontal sinus with extension to the anterior cranial fossa. Short tau inversion recovery (STIR), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) showing diffusion restriction as well as enhancement and thickening of dura mater (white arrows).
in_text_mentions: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed enhancement of the lesion in T2-weighted images, whereas in T1 there was ring enhancement characteristic of a mature abscess (Figure 2).
